changesets.title: THE SCIENCE IS NO JOKE
changesets.notes: Published Apr 1. Science-led April Fools email — Machado 2022 qEEG study. 7-day measurement window through Apr 8. Brief updated with final creative at publish.

actual_impact.primary_metric_delta: -$4,816.39 vs $6K target (-80.3%); however, within normal range ($874–$2,123) for comparable non-promotional content emails

_detail.campaign_name: UE | C1/M19 - The Science is no joke
_detail.benchmark_note: Against 7 comparable non-promo content emails (Mar-Apr 2026): open rate #1 (46.5% vs 41.5% avg), click rate #1 (0.71% vs 0.64% avg), CTOR top 3 (1.52% vs 1.56% avg). Revenue mid-range ($1,184 vs $1,908 avg for revenue-generating sends).

actual_impact._note: margin_impact = $1,183.61 × 50% DTC Shopify margin = $591.81. Classified as underperformed vs original $6K target, but targets were misset — $6K and 8% CTR were promotional-campaign benchmarks applied to a non-promotional science engagement email. Actual performance led comparable content emails on engagement metrics.
actual_impact.L1_margin_actual: Below vs original target ($592 vs $3,000). However, target was based on promotional benchmarks — comparable content email margin range is $437–$1,061.
actual_impact.L3_customer_quality_actual: Inconclusive — 15 conversions too few to assess quality. $78.91 AOV is consistent with standard DTC orders.
actual_impact.L4_learning_actual: Hypothesis partially supported: science subject lines generate top-of-class opens (46.5%, #1 in set). CTOR of 1.52% is in line with content emails, not elevated. Key insight: science credibility hooks open emails effectively but don't differentially drive clicks vs other content themes. The original 8% CTR target was based on promotional campaigns with offers, not content emails. Future science emails should be benchmarked against content-email baselines (~0.6% click rate, ~1.5% CTOR, ~$1K-$2K revenue for ~17K sends).

changesets.learning_note: Science-led April Fools email sent to 17K (not 51K — standard suppressions) → $1,184 revenue, 46.5% open rate (#1 in class), 0.71% click rate (#1 in class), 1.52% CTOR → Revenue underperformed vs $6K target but target was misset: $6K and 8% CTR were promo benchmarks, not content-email benchmarks. Actual performance led all comparable non-promo sends on engagement. Correct baseline for non-promo science emails: ~$1K-$2K revenue, ~0.6% click rate, ~1.5% CTOR.

changesets.title: Claims Audit — KME Endurance & MCT:Glucose Ratio (Martyn/Frenser 2026)

expected_impact.primary_metric_target: Zero blanket KME endurance claims + all MCT:glucose SKUs reviewed by Apr 20

changesets.notes: D16 Martyn et al. 2026 (J Appl Physiol, PMID 41962970, n=8 RCT) directly contradicts universal KME endurance claims — benefit is metabolic-state-conditional, not universal. D16 Frenser 2026 (Sci Rep, PMID 41957196) documents MCT:glucose ketogenesis threshold (1.5g glucose per 1g MCT); carb-forward Kenetik SKUs may violate. D17 FTC enforcement wave on MetaTrim + Jelly Lean BHB claims creates regulatory context. Scope: (1) audit all social/email/paid KME performance claims for metabolic-state specificity; (2) review MCT:glucose ratio across SKUs; (3) update claims-compliance.md with science-contradiction workflow. Blocks unsafe content advancement on 10 idea-status posts.
